content:
- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.7) — reduce forecast peak by 2–5% relative to sentiment intensity.
- Underestimate prices during low sentiment (sentiment < 0.3) — add 1–3% to forecast to compensate for mean reversion bias.
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes (e.g., >7% from prior day) — cap forecast at 10% above prior peak to avoid overcorrection.
- Lagged price movements (forecast 30d vs true 30d) show persistent underestimation of late-period rallies — adjust final 5–7 days upward by 1–2% per day.
- When sentiment is rising but price is flat or falling, reduce forecast slope — avoid “sentiment-driven” overbought extrapolation.
- Forecast mean reversion bias is strongest in early 30d — apply 1–2% downward correction to first 10 days if sentiment is neutral or declining.
